goal: Speed up block validation and IBD by batch-verifying Schnorr signatures instead of checking them one at a time
Aims to help every node operator's sync time on taproot-heavy blocks, though the net win is still unproven
reviewability: Paused: author says rebasing doesn't make sense until upstream secp256k1 batch module stabilizes
Marked EXPERIMENTAL by the author, meant for design discussion rather than merge review right now
agreement: No concept objections to batch verification itself, reviewers engaged substantively (andrewtoth, Eunovo, 0xB10C, willcl-ark)
Unaddressed objection: early benchmark showed the approach was slower than master, even post-taproot (0xB10C, willcl-ark)
Nonblocking objection: lock contention in the shared-batch design, prompted a redesign (andrewtoth, Eunovo)
Verified by testing: redesigned per-thread approach faster than master at high thread counts, though testing was ongoing (Eunovo)
Author himself treats net performance benefit as unresolved pending secp256k1 pippenger work (fjahr)

categories.name: utils
why: P3 because it adds a large vendored secp256k1 batch module and reworks checkqueue.h threading with a real but unproven performance goal
Capped below P2 since the upstream secp256k1 batch module it depends on is itself unmerged and still changing
Value today is mainly as a discussion vehicle for future speedups rather than a stable utility improvement

categories.name: validation
why: P3 because faster block validation would be a widely felt benefit for node operators if it works out
Measured benefit is inconsistent so far, an early version was slower than master and later redesigns only partially validated
Not reaching P2 because the author explicitly does not propose this for merge yet and it rests on an unstable upstream API
